title: A lesson in Chat
viewerNote: Keating’s replies are scripted. The progress rail shows its stage labels with independent review turned off.

steps.title: Ask Keating
steps.explanation: Type a concrete learning question in Message Keating. Send it to start the lesson.
steps.alt: The chat composer contains Teach me how recursion returns.

steps.title: Follow the reply
steps.explanation: The progress rail names the stages of the turn. The tutor starts by asking for a prediction.
steps.alt: Keating's progress rail shows Draft, Review and Reply.

steps.title: Make a prediction
steps.explanation: Choose the first answer and send it. Keating responds with a hint and asks you to think again.
steps.alt: The first choice is selected in the recursion quick check.

steps.text: Make a prediction in the quick check.
What happens to that first call while the second one returns?

steps.title: Try the question again
steps.explanation: Choose The first call waits and send your answer. Keating explains where the waiting call resumes.
steps.alt: The second quick check has The first call waits selected.

steps.text: Try the check again after the hint.
The call stack gives each call a place to wait.

steps.title: Reveal a flashcard
steps.explanation: Reveal the card, compare your recall with the answer, and rate it Good.
steps.alt: A revealed flashcard explains where a recursive call waits.

steps.text: Reveal the answer and rate your recall.

steps.title: Run the countdown
steps.explanation: Run tests executes the starter function with the sample inputs. Read both results in the code activity.
steps.alt: The countdown coding activity with its sample test results.

steps.title: Read the sources
steps.explanation: The Sources footer names the references for the reply. You can return to them after the exercise.
steps.alt: The Sources footer links to MDN’s recursion and call stack entries.

steps.title: Use a study chip
steps.explanation: Explain another way adds a follow-up to the composer. Read the suggested wording before you send.
steps.alt: The composer has the suggested follow-up from Explain another way.

steps.text: Explain another way drafts a follow-up.

steps.title: Notice the failed reply
steps.explanation: The scripted demo tutor interrupts the reply. Your question stays in the conversation.
steps.alt: The failed response offers a Retry response button.

steps.text: The reply failed. Your question is still here.

steps.title: Retry the reply
steps.explanation: Retry response sends the same request again. The scripted tutor replies with a folder-tree example.
steps.alt: A completed tutor reply explains the folder-tree example.

steps.text: Retry the turn to continue the lesson.
A folder tree is another example.

to.label: A folder tree is another example.
